flags: Taxonomy forced: the question straddles two topics -- statement I is about expressing the strength of hydrogen peroxide ('volume strength'), statement II is water of crystallization in CuSO4.5H2O. Filed on statement II; no catalog subtopic covers volume strength.

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements :
I. The leaves of nettle, a herbaceous plant, cause painful stings when touched accidentally because of the secretion of formic acid.
II. When gypsum is heated at \(100^\circ\text{C}\), it forms calcium carbonate hemihydrate, called Plaster of Paris.
III. When moistened with water, anhydrous copper sulphate forms a green-coloured copper sulphate dihydrate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct ?
questions.subject: Chemistry
flags: Transcribed as printed: statement II says 'calcium carbonate hemihydrate' (the page really does read carbonate, not sulphate) and statement III says 'green-coloured ... dihydrate'. Both read as deliberate distractor errors in the printed paper; not repaired.
